extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers of scientific method / historians of science / experimentalists interested in Baconian methodology
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying Francis Bacon's taxonomy of 'instances' (praerogatives) for designing, measuring, and reasoning from experiments — i.e., the methodological criteria Bacon gives for discovering and testing natural causes. Focuses on types of instances, substitution strategies, measurement instances, and practical constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantias Supplementi, sive Substitutionis
rubrics_metrics.description: “Eae sunt, quae supplent informationem ubi sensus plane destituitur; atque idcirco ad eas confugimus cum instantiae propriae haberi non possint.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when direct sensible instances are unavailable — supplement information in place of proper instances. Can be employed when proper instances are lacking or additionally alongside proper instances to strengthen information. Two main modes (per gradus and per analoga) are described; substitution can suggest candidate media or models for testing but must be applied with caution and later checked by direct instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitutio per Gradus (substitution by degrees)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Talis est substitutio quae fit per Gradus.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute by comparing degrees/gradations of related sensible bodies (e.g., test many candidate media to find one that weakens a magnet's action comparatively and by degree). This mode is relatively more certain: experiment across a graded series to infer comparative effects. Example: testing various media (gold, silver, stone, glass, wood, air, flame) to find relative inhibition of magnetism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitutio per Analoga (substitution by analogy)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Substitutio autem per Analoga, utilis sane, sed minus certa est; atque idcirco cum judicio quodam adhibenda. Ea fit, cum deducitur non-sensibile ad sensum ... per contemplationem corporis alicujus cognati sensibilis.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infer properties of non-sensible (invisible) bodies by contemplation of cognate sensible bodies — useful but less certain than gradational substitution. Requires applied judgment and should be treated as suggestive hypothesis that needs verification. Examples: reasoning about 'mixture of spirits' by analogy with mixtures of water and oil, or using electrical models to illustrate muscle electricity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantias Persecantes / Vellicantes (prodding/persecuting instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Eae sunt, quae de admirabili et exquisita subtilitate naturae intellectum submonent, ut excitetur et expergiscatur ad attentionem et observationem et inquisitionem debitam.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instances that attract attention to extremely subtle or minute phenomena so they are noticed and investigated. Examples: minute spread of ink over many letters, extremely fine wire-drawing, tiny differences in odor or color, delicate distinctions of articulated sound through porous substances. Use to awaken close observation and prompt further inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantias Metas Persecationis (meta-persecution instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Solemus tamen utiliter hujusmodi instantiis persecutihus subjungere instantias, quas Metas Persecutionis appellare consuevimus; veluti quod in iis, quae diximus, una actio in diverso genere aliam non perturbet aut impediat ...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instances used to test whether different simultaneous actions interfere with one another (non-interference tests). Useful for demonstrating that one action in a different genus does not impede another, or conversely showing dominant/antagonistic relations. They help reveal separable pathways or independent channels of action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantias quae juvant sensum / Partes Informativae
rubrics_metrics.description: “Atque de instantiis quae juvant sensum, jam dictum est; quae praecipui usus sunt ad Partem Informativam. Informatio enim incipit a sensu.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instances that aid the senses are the starting point of informative inquiry — gather clear sensible observations first. These are foundational for building up to operative experiments and further inference. Emphasis that knowledge begins with sense-perception, which then leads to operative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantias Practicas (practical/operative instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Sequentur itaque instantiae praecipui usus ad partem operativam. Eae genere duae sunt, numero septem; ... Operativae autem partis, vitia duo; totidemque dignitates instantiarum in genere. Aut enim fallit operatio, aut onerat nimis.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instances relevant to the practical (operative) part of inquiry. Practical work is liable to two defects: operations may fail, or practice may be too onerous. Practical instances should therefore be selected to avoid failure and excessive cost/effort; they should direct action toward the most important ends and be feasible to implement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantias Mathematicae / Instantias Mensurae (mathematical / measuring instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Instantias vero quatuor ... uno nomine Instantias Mathematicas vocamus, et Instantias Mensnrae.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instances that measure nature — by space (gradus spatii) or by time (momenta temporis) — and provide quantitative data. Examples and instruments: thermometer, barometer, hygrometer, goniometer, micrometer, scales, photometer, electrometer, thermo-electric pile, methods like double-weighing or coincidences. These are crucial for enabling reliable generalization and theoretical demonstration; experiments must afford accurate measures of the quantities concerned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantias Propitias / Benevolae (propitious or benevolent instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Itiaque eae instantiae in pretio esse debent, quae aut dirigunt operativam ad ea quae maxime hominum intersunt; aut quae parcunt instrumentis; aut quae parcunt materiae sive supellectili. Eas autem tres instantias ... Instantias Propitias sive Benevolas vocamus.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical instances valued because they reduce burden: (1) direct operations toward what most concerns humans (utility), (2) spare instruments (economy of apparatus), (3) spare material/supplies. Prefer such instances to avoid onerous practice and to make operative work feasible and relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantias Virgae / Radii / Perlationis / Non Ultra (rod/radius / limits instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Instantias Virgae, sive Radii, Perlationis, vel de Non Ultra appellare consuevimus. Virtutes enim rerum et motus operantur et expediuntur per spatia non indefinita aut fortuita, sed finita et certa; quae ... plurimum interest practicae ... ut magis sit aucta et potens.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instances that determine how virtues/powers operate across space (range, reach, and finite limits). Important to note exact distances, limits ('Non Ultra'), and the spatial extent of effects (e.g., magnetism range, odor travel, light/radiation). Compute and note quantities: distances, vigor, strengths, and impediments of media. These are essential for practical work and for understanding effective ranges of phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mensurae motuum localium et missilium (measures of local and projectile motions)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Quinctiam mensurae motuum violentorum (quos vocant), ut missilium, tormentorum, rotarum, et similium, cum hae quoque manifesto suos habeant limites certos, notandae sunt.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure violent/local motions (projectiles, artillery, rotating bodies) and determine their definite limits. Note distances at which percussion/impact is effective; these measurable limits are important for practical applications and for preventing mistaken operation due to unmeasured ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mensurae motuum sphaericorum (measures of spherical/expansive-contractive motions)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Est et aliud genus mensurae localis motuum, quod non praetermittendum est. Illud vero pertinet ad motus non progressivos, sed sphaericos; hoc est, ad expansionem corporum in majorem sphaeram, aut contractionem in minorem.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure how bodies expand or contract (spherical/volumetric changes) and determine how much compression/extension bodies endure before reaching a 'Non Ultra' limit. Text gives specific experimental procedures (bell in water, egg-with-hole vacuum experiment, lead globe compressed by hammering) to probe compressibility and elasticity. Be mindful of experimental artefacts (e.g., water exuding through lead pores) and interpret results cautiously.
